findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: No certified food protection manager (CFPM) was available during the inspection. The inspector advised the person-in-charge (PIC) to get certified in food protection management so that a CFPM is available during all hours of food preparation/operation. The director of the program is certified but shares some time with Nokomis schools. See that more than one person is certified within the facility. Operator present during the inspection has a certificate that just expired on March 2. She intends to retake the course and test sometime within the next week.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. The facility dish machine operator had no knowledge of testing the heat sanitizing dish machine using a maximum registering thermometer. An image of the device was shared with the dish operator. See that the facility purchases and uses (daily) the thermometer to insure the accuracy of the dish machine. Operator knew to check the display to ensure the rinse temperature was at least 180F.
(A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [PF]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The fan cover in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation. The PIC was informed to ensure the fan cover is cleaned to sight and touch and kept free of dust. Furthermore, the two box fans being used in the facility (dish and kitchen) are also observed soiled. See that these fans are cleaned prior to use. Do not allow soiled air to flow over the kitchen space.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. No food handler cards were available for present staff. Only one employee was recently hired. See that all staff are either certified food managers or food handlers as required. There should be one certified food managers present during all hours of operations. Anyone else should have the food handlers card. 

(b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed there were dented cans on the dry storage shelf in the back of the kitchen. The PIC stated that employees should be putting any dented cans they find when stocking shelves in the office. During the inspection the cans were removed from service and brought to the office. Ensure that food packages are always in good condition to protect food from exposure to potential contaminants.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer dispenser (sink and surface sanitizer; lactic acid) at the triple sink in the back of the kitchen is not pulling any sanitizer through the line and only dispensing water. During the inspection the PIC manually made a sanitizer bucket testing at the correct concentration. The inspector will follow-up on 9/22/2025 to ensure that the sanitizer dispenser is dispensing at the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed there is an accumulation of frost inside the white standing freezer in the back of the kitchen. The freezer must be de-frosted to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the cove base behind the dish washing machine is missing or peeling off the wall. The missing cove base must be replaced and the peeling cove base must be sealed to the wall. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed that the facility has Quat and Lactic Acid test strips available but they use Chlorine sanitizer (bleach). The inspector educated about the importance of using the correct type of test strip to ensure that sanitizer buckets are the proper concentration. The inspector had an extra package of Chlorine test strips which were provided to the facility during the inspection. The PIC will be purchasing more of the correct test strips as well. Ensure test kits are always available to accurately measure the concentration of sanitizing solutions.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
The employees currently in the kitchen are both handler certified. There is no certified food protection manager, CFPM, in the facility. Ensure that there are enough certified managers employed so that the kitchen is under the management of a CFPM at all times. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed employee begin to don gloves without first doing any sort of hand washing. The employee was stopped and coached concerning proper hand washing and glove use.  The sign for proper hand washing was reviewed and the employee did use a barrier to turn off the handles of the faucet. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The leak in the ceiling over the stainless counter side of the serving windows is back. The facility is scheduled for a roof repair to start as soon as the students are done with school. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The facility does not utilize sanitizer on the tables in the cafeteria. The facility shall ensure that food contact surfaces are sanitized. Sanitizers shall meet code requirements and have labeling consistent with use for food contact surfaces. The facility will use chlorine bleach at 100ppm to sanitize. A follow up will be conducted tomorrow 3/29/24 before service.  
4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
The facility had a fly strip hanging over the clean dish drain board. The fly strip was removed. Take care not to hang fly strips over areas that need to be kept clean. Protect clean areas from contamination. The violation was corrected on site. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no CFPM for the facility. CFPM licenses expired during the COVID-19 pandemic. Re-taking the course and exam has been discussed during previous inspections. SCDPH Food Program Manager’s card was given to PIC in order to proctor the exam. PIC, Karen, stated the employees would like to take the course online; however, SCDPH can proctor the exam. Ensure CFPM course and exam are re-taken before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

Observed caulk at dish machine to still be coming away from wall. Discussed repairs with PIC and maintenance man. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/28/20.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Caulk at dish machine area were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed caulk at dish machine area to be coming from the wall. Discussed re-caulking with PIC.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Interior of ice machine appears soiled with accumulation of white substance. Staff has agreed to contact maintenance company to service the machine. Table top can opener found soiled with food debris at the time of inspection. Can opener was sanitized at the time of inspection. 
->Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. (Reference 4-601.11(A))

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Unlabeled spray bottle of bleach solution found stored under shelf near dish machine. Bottle was labeled at the time of inspection.
->Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. (Reference 7-102.11.)

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Thermometer guage on the dish machine was found reading 171F after 3 cycles. A heat strip placed on metal pan indicated a temperature change and vertified water temperature greater than 160F. 
-> Thermometer used by the high temperature dish machine is not calibrated. Must be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. (Reference 4-502.11(B).)

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Hand sink in the back of the kitchen was found non-operational. Facility stated they are using a secondary 3-compartment sink as a back-up handsink until handsink is repaired. Staff indicated handsink will be repaired during spring break to avoid water interuptions during lunch service.
->Repair according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  (Reference 5-205.15.)
